headline: Grow a game into the world around you.
intro: Ann Arbor Go connects map exploration with phone-based AR: plant trees on detected surfaces, revisit them, and explore the surrounding landmarks.
context: University of Michigan · XR course project · Oct 2022
role: I co-developed the game with Maxwell Zuber, contributing mode/navigation UI, camera setup, and acorn interactions. We shared implementation rather than assigning fixed subsystems.

hero.alt: An illustrated map-exploration scene and phone AR scene connected by shared inventory and planted-tree state.
hero.caption: System illustration drawn from the original C# source. This is not a screenshot of the mobile build.
hero.credit: Original project: Le Qin and Maxwell Zuber

question.title: What makes a virtual tree feel part of a place?
question.text: A game needs more than a model on the camera view. Placement, navigation, and remembered state must fit together as the player moves between local interaction and wider exploration.

steps.title: Explore the area
steps.text: Navigate a map with compass and landmark cues. A teammate-proposed drone mode lets players scout before traveling.

steps.title: Interact in AR
steps.text: Place seeds at the AR cursor and interact with trees; acorns serve as projectiles for squirrel defense.

steps.title: Carry state forward
steps.text: Retain inventory and transfer planted-tree information between interaction and exploration scenes.

finding.title: Test the real device early.
finding.text: Phone deployment problems delayed testing, and movement that felt fast in the editor felt slow on-device. The project made regular hardware testing a concrete development lesson.

details: The original is a solo game built by two teammates. Cross-scene state is not multiplayer synchronization.
The browser scene is an illustrative reconstruction. Its water/boost actions and simplified growth stages are not a reproduction of the original mobile mechanics.
credits: Built with Unity, C#, AR Foundation, and Mapbox. The original team recording remains linked below.
Project source, commit history, and Le Qin's course postmortem support this account.
